levels.C: Compatible: reads another host's format, or available via config
levels.P: Partial: opt-in, limited to some interfaces, or reduced

capabilities.label: Terminal CLI / TUI
capabilities.strategy: Not a portability concern; note which interface you tested on, because features differ between them.

capabilities.label: IDE (editor or extension)
capabilities.strategy: Test IDE and CLI separately; Copilot's VS Code Local harness and the CLI differ materially.

capabilities.label: Cloud / background agent
capabilities.strategy: Cloud agents run the repo harness remotely; anything that depends on user-level config will be missing.

capabilities.label: Headless run from a script (prompt in, exit)
capabilities.strategy: Per-host eval adapter around the headless command; one CI job can test a tool in every host.

capabilities.label: Headless with machine-readable (JSON) output
capabilities.strategy: Parse JSON output in the eval adapter to record skill activation and outcomes.

capabilities.label: Reads AGENTS.md
capabilities.strategy: Author AGENTS.md as the source of truth; add one line of glue where a host needs it.

capabilities.label: Reads CLAUDE.md
capabilities.strategy: CLAUDE.md = '@AGENTS.md' plus Claude-only notes; avoids double loading in hosts that cross-read.

capabilities.label: Own always-on instruction file (host-specific name)
capabilities.strategy: Generate a one-line wrapper pointing at AGENTS.md rather than duplicating content.

capabilities.label: Per-folder (nested) instruction files
capabilities.strategy: Nested AGENTS.md plus generated wrappers; check each host's loading direction.

capabilities.label: Inline @-imports of other files
capabilities.strategy: Summarise inline and link the detail; never depend on inlining.

capabilities.label: Triggered rules scoped by file glob
capabilities.strategy: One neutral rule source generated per host; fold into nested AGENTS.md where there are no rules.

capabilities.label: Rules activated by description (model decides)
capabilities.strategy: Prefer a skill: same activation model, portable format.

capabilities.label: Skills in .agents/skills
capabilities.strategy: Canonical .agents/skills; deliver .claude/skills as a link or copy for Claude Code.

capabilities.label: Skills in .claude/skills
capabilities.strategy: Second delivery folder; watch for double discovery in hosts that read both.

capabilities.label: Agent Skills spec (SKILL.md, progressive disclosure)
capabilities.strategy: Six spec fields only, actor-neutral wording, lint in CI because invalid skills fail silently.

capabilities.label: Host-specific skill frontmatter extensions
capabilities.strategy: Extras are P3; generate them per target, never in the canonical SKILL.md.

capabilities.label: User commands as their own format
capabilities.strategy: Author as skills; generate command files only for hosts that still need them.

capabilities.label: Agent profiles (named sub-agents)
capabilities.strategy: Neutral agent-profile YAML fed to generators.

capabilities.label: Agent profile can restrict its tools
capabilities.strategy: Generators warn, never silently widen, when a target can't express tool limits.

capabilities.label: Reads another host's agent-profile folder
capabilities.strategy: Useful fallback, but generate native files so behaviour is explicit.

capabilities.label: Shell-command hooks (event count in note)
capabilities.strategy: One hook core plus a thin adapter per host.

capabilities.label: Event: session.start
capabilities.strategy: Part of the portable four-event coverage.

capabilities.label: Event: tool.before
capabilities.strategy: Part of the portable four-event coverage. Re-filter inside the core, because matchers aren't portable.

capabilities.label: Event: tool.after
capabilities.strategy: Part of the portable four-event coverage.

capabilities.label: Event: agent.stop
capabilities.strategy: Part of the portable four-event coverage.

capabilities.label: Hook can block a tool call
capabilities.strategy: Adapter refuses to install a guard where the host can't block; every guard also has a gate.

capabilities.label: Hook can inject context
capabilities.strategy: Declare canInjectContext per adapter.

capabilities.label: Hook can rewrite tool input
capabilities.strategy: Declare canRewriteInput per adapter; don't depend on it.

capabilities.label: Hook can rewrite tool output
capabilities.strategy: Declare canRewriteOutput per adapter; don't depend on it.

capabilities.label: Model-level hooks (before/after model call)
capabilities.strategy: Host-exclusive; no portable equivalent.

capabilities.label: Inferential hook handlers (prompt/agent)
capabilities.strategy: Host-exclusive; use a command handler for portability.

capabilities.label: Hooks can be configured or default to fail closed
capabilities.strategy: Declare open/closed per hook; the wrapper enforces it; every guard has a gate.

capabilities.label: Reads Claude Code hook configuration
capabilities.strategy: Don't rely on cross-reads for guards; generate native config.

capabilities.label: Allow / ask / deny permission rules
capabilities.strategy: Neutral policy.yaml fed to generators; enforcement lives in the sandbox and gates.

capabilities.label: Permissions can be committed in the repo
capabilities.strategy: Where they can't, document the user-level setup and rely on gates.

capabilities.label: OS-level sandbox
capabilities.strategy: Containers or devcontainers for real, portable isolation.

capabilities.label: Ignore list that actually holds
capabilities.strategy: Treat ignore files as advisory everywhere; real enforcement is sandbox or managed policy.

capabilities.label: Org / enterprise managed policy
capabilities.strategy: Per host; tell users what is enforcement and what is advisory.

capabilities.label: MCP client
capabilities.strategy: Wrap capabilities as MCP servers; every host gets the same tool.

capabilities.label: Project-level MCP config file (path in note)
capabilities.strategy: Neutral servers.yaml generated per host; pinned stdio subset; env-var names only.

capabilities.label: Remote (HTTP) MCP servers
capabilities.strategy: Wire remote servers and secrets per host.

capabilities.label: Language-server tool exposed to the model
capabilities.strategy: Wrap code intelligence as an MCP server instead.

capabilities.label: Automatic memory across sessions
capabilities.strategy: Tool-local; durable facts belong in AGENTS.md.

capabilities.label: Plugin / extension packages
capabilities.strategy: Generate two manifests: Agent Plugins and Claude's.

capabilities.label: Marketplace / catalog
capabilities.strategy: Git-hosted catalogs; test install per host because parts are dropped silently.

capabilities.label: Agent Plugins 1.0 client
capabilities.strategy: Only skills and MCP travel in the standard's scope.

capabilities.label: Reads Claude plugin manifest (.claude-plugin/)
capabilities.strategy: A Claude manifest reaches several hosts; still test each.

hosts.label: Claude Code
hosts.summary: Has the most hooks of any tool (33 events, 5 handler types), plus path-scoped rules and skills that can fork into subagents. Other tools often read its formats. It reads AGENTS.md only in some cases and ignores .agents/skills.

unique.title: 33 hook events, 5 handler types
unique.detail: Handlers can be command, http, mcp_tool, prompt or (experimental) agent. updatedToolOutput works for any tool, PreToolUse can defer, and PermissionRequest hooks can supply updatedInput.

unique.title: Skills that fork and carry hooks
unique.detail: Skills can run in a subagent (context: fork), pre-approve tools, ship their own hooks, inject live shell output with ! blocks, and scope by paths.

unique.title: Auto permission mode
unique.detail: In auto mode a classifier (Sonnet 5 by default) reviews actions. Since v2.1.283 it is the built-in starting mode for interactive sessions, but not for claude -p or the Agent SDK. There is also dontAsk, and a sandbox that protects credentials. Anthropic reports 93% of prompts approved.

unique.title: Subagent isolation and memory
unique.detail: Worktree isolation, per-agent persistent memory, per-agent hooks and MCP scoping, depth 3 / concurrency 20 limits, --agent main-session mode.

unique.title: Plugins with dependencies and monitors
unique.detail: userConfig with secure storage, dependencies, monitors, LSP servers, bin on PATH, seven plugin source types, org policy over marketplaces.

unique.title: Cloud, teleport and scheduling
unique.detail: Cloud sessions, --teleport, Remote Control, Channels, cloud scheduled tasks (formerly routines), /loop, auto-fix PRs, agent teams.

unique.title: Claude as MCP server and SDK
unique.detail: claude mcp serve exposes Claude Code as an MCP server. The Agent SDK (Python, TypeScript) runs the same engine and loads .claude/ config.

gotchas: AGENTS.md is skipped if any CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists on the path, even a tiny one. Use a CLAUDE.md that contains @AGENTS.md.
Does not read .agents/skills. Put skills in .claude/skills as a link or copy.
Hooks fail open by default: a mistyped path or exit 1 won't block. Only exit 2 (blocking events), valid deny JSON or onFailure: "block" (command/http, v2.1.295+) blocks.
claude -p and cloud sessions run repo hooks and .mcp.json servers with no trust prompt unless --bare.
Glob and Grep are off by default, so a Grep|Glob hook matcher never fires. Searches arrive as Bash calls.
Cloud sessions ignore ~/.claude and user-only plugins. Commit skills and settings to the repo.
The managed-only Project instructions setting drops project CLAUDE.md, breaking the @AGENTS.md wrapper.

surface.cli.note: Interactive terminal CLI; all interfaces share one engine, so CLAUDE.md, settings and MCP work across them.

surface.ide.note: Extensions for VS Code and JetBrains plus a desktop app; same engine and config as the CLI.

surface.cloud.note: Managed VMs read repo .claude/ (settings, agents, skills, hooks) but NOT ~/.claude or user-only plugins; LSP servers do not start. A thread in a claude.ai Project loads only root CLAUDE.md and non-path-scoped rules, with no repo hooks, skills or agents.

headless.run.note: Same engine as the Agent SDK; --bare skips auto-discovery and is recommended for CI. Without --bare it runs project hooks and .mcp.json without trust prompts.

headless.json.note: json gives result, session_id, cost; stream-json is NDJSON; system/init event lists plugins, MCP servers and capabilities.

instr.agents-md.note: Read only when no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists on the path; else needs @AGENTS.md. Never reads AGENTS.override.md or .agents/.

instr.claude-md.note: Managed, user, project and local tiers; delivered as a user message, context not enforcement.

instr.own-file.note: Its own always-on file; recommended bridge is CLAUDE.md containing @AGENTS.md plus Claude-only notes.

instr.nested.note: Ancestors load at launch; subdirectory files load on demand when Claude reads files there. Nested AGENTS.md only if the dir has no CLAUDE.md. Capped at 40,000 chars (200K window) or 150,000 to 200,000 (1M window) since v2.1.309.

instr.imports.note: Recursive to 4 hops; skipped in code blocks; imports outside cwd need one-time approval; loaded at launch, so no context saving.

rules.glob.note: Only frontmatter field is paths; rules without paths load at launch. Path-scoped rules trigger when Claude reads or edits a matching file (Read, Write, Edit, or a single-file Bash read).

rules.description.note: No description-activated rules; use a skill (description-based) instead.

skills.agents-dir.note: Claude Code does not read .agents/skills (re-checked raw 2026-09-29); the only core host that does not.

skills.claude-dir.note: Enterprise > personal > project precedence; nested .claude/skills auto-discovered; plugin skills namespaced /plugin:skill.

skills.spec.note: All fields optional, only description recommended; license, compatibility, metadata accepted; listing budget 1% of context, 1,536 chars per skill.

skills.extras.native: context: fork, paths, allowed-tools, hooks, when_to_use, effort...
skills.extras.note: Many extras beyond the six spec fields; unknown fields ignored without a warning.

commands.format.note: Still works but merged into skills (a file and a skill dir both create /name); prefer skills for new work.

agents.profiles.note: Markdown plus YAML; only name and description required; subagents with worktree isolation, memory, hooks, MCP scoping and a per-agent autoCompactWindow (v2.1.296+).

agents.tool-limits.note: Allowlist and denylist per agent; plugin agents may not use hooks, mcpServers or permissionMode.

agents.cross-read.note: Does not read other hosts' agent folders; /import (v2.1.213+) copies another agent's config once.

hooks.shell.note: 33 events, five handler types: command, http, mcp_tool, prompt, agent (experimental).

hooks.session-start.note: Plain stdout or additionalContext becomes context; SessionEnd, Setup also exist.

hooks.tool-before.note: permissionDecision allow|deny|ask|defer, updatedInput, additionalContext; exit 2 blocks before rules run.

hooks.tool-after.note: Can replace tool output; exit 2 is not honoured here since the tool already ran.

hooks.agent-stop.note: decision block keeps the agent going; exit 2 blocks.

hooks.block.note: Exit 2 blocks only on events marked Yes; a deny/ask permission rule still wins over a hook allow. Tested in 2.1.310: exit 1, a timeout and a missing script fail open; onFailure: block makes them block.

hooks.inject-context.note: Capped at 10,000 chars (overflow spills to a file); available on SessionStart, PreToolUse, Stop, SubagentStart and more.

hooks.rewrite-output.note: All tools since v2.1.121; changes only what Claude sees. updatedMCPToolOutput is the older MCP-only field.

hooks.model-level.note: No before/after model-call hooks; nearest are PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch (model switch only) and UserPromptSubmit.

hooks.inferential.note: Prompt hooks return ok/reason; agent hooks are experimental and unsupported on PermissionRequest.

hooks.fail-closed.note: Per-hook opt-in: a hook that cannot start, times out, exits other than 0/2 or prints invalid JSON then blocks; default is "continue" (fail open). No effect on Stop, SubagentStop, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle or async hooks.

hooks.cross-read.note: Claude is the source format that Cursor, Copilot CLI and (opt-in) VS Code read; it reads no other host's hooks.

policy.rules.note: Order deny, ask, allow; first match wins; specificity does not matter. Modes include plan, auto (classifier), dontAsk. Auto is the built-in starting mode for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions since v2.1.283; claude -p, the Agent SDK, disableAutoMode and HIPAA start in default.

policy.repo.note: Committed project rules; allow rules and hooks follow workspace trust; .claude/settings.local.json for personal overrides.

policy.sandbox.note: macOS Seatbelt, Linux/WSL2 bubblewrap; covers Bash and children; failIfUnavailable defaults to warn and run unsandboxed.

policy.ignore.note: No ignore file. Read deny covers cat/head/tail/sed/tee and redirects but not grep -r; OS-level needs sandbox denyRead.

policy.managed.note: Highest precedence; managed CLAUDE.md cannot be excluded; managed hooks cannot be disabled from lower levels.

mcp.client.note: stdio, http (recommended), sse (deprecated), ws; scopes local, project, user.

mcp.project-config.note: Root-level {mcpServers}; project servers need approval interactively, but -p and cloud load them without prompting. Duplicate-name precedence: managedMcpServers > local > project > user > plugin > claude.ai connectors.

mcp.remote.native: type: http, url, headers, headersHelper, oauth
mcp.remote.note: ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} expansion; credential vars read as empty in remote url/headers.

intel.lsp.note: Plugin-only: no repo-level LSP config outside a plugin; not started in cloud sessions. Also diagnostics after each edit.

intel.memory.note: On by default; first 200 lines/25 KB loaded; machine-local; subagents do not inherit it (forks do).

plugins.package.note: Bundles skills, commands, agents, hooks, MCP, LSP, monitors, bin; only name required; userConfig and dependencies supported.

plugins.marketplace.note: Seven plugin source types; add from GitHub, git URL, local path or hosted JSON; strictKnownMarketplaces allowlist for orgs.

plugins.agent-plugins.note: Not listed as an Agent Plugins 1.0 compatible client; whether it will load them natively is an open question.

plugins.claude-manifest.note: The source format. Also read by VS Code Copilot, Copilot CLI and Codex; Codex path confirmed in source.

hosts.label: OpenAI Codex
hosts.summary: Codex is built around the sandbox. Sandbox mode and approval policy are separate, and execpolicy rules are testable. Hooks work much like Claude's but need a trust review. Agent profiles are TOML, with Claude plugin manifests as a fallback.

unique.title: Sandbox x approval axes
unique.detail: Sandbox mode and approval policy are set independently, with granular approvals and an auto_review (Guardian) reviewer. Permission profiles support extends and network domain rules.

unique.title: execpolicy Starlark rules
unique.detail: prefix_rule() with match/not_match self-tests, checked with 'codex execpolicy check'. The most restrictive rule wins. These rules are command policy, not instructions.

unique.title: Hash-keyed hook trust
unique.detail: Hooks that are not managed must be approved in /hooks, and the approval is tied to a hash of the hook definition. Untrusted projects skip project .codex layers. Managed hooks skip review.

unique.title: AGENTS.override.md
unique.detail: Per-directory local override plus configurable fallback filenames, under a 32 KiB combined cap.

unique.title: mcp_tool and async hooks
unique.detail: Hook handler type mcp_tool, async command hooks (max 8), Interrupt event, and spill files for oversized hook context.

unique.title: Per-agent TOML
unique.detail: Agent TOML sets model, model_reasoning_effort (up to ultra), skill config and feature switches. Sandbox, approvals and MCP servers are inherited from the parent.

unique.title: GitHub Action and SDKs
unique.detail: openai/codex-action with safety-strategy, TypeScript and Python SDKs (Python drives the app-server). codex mcp-server was removed.

unique.title: Reads Claude and Cursor marketplaces
unique.detail: Marketplace lookup includes .claude-plugin/ and .cursor-plugin/ files, and sets CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT for plugin hooks.

gotchas: In Codex, .codex/rules/*.rules is command policy (prefix_rule), not instructions. Do not generate instruction rules there.
Hook matchers have no Read or Grep tools, so file reads show up as Bash. Hosted web_search fires no hooks.
Unsupported hook outputs (ask, updatedMCPToolOutput, empty-reason deny) fail open and the tool call proceeds.
Hook prompt and agent handlers are skipped silently, so Claude hook files load and do nothing.
Hooks and project .codex config need trust review (/hooks); CI needs managed hooks or --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust.
AGENTS.md stops loading files at 32 KiB combined (project_doc_max_bytes), with no imports or globs. The docs have moved to learn.chatgpt.com/docs.

surface.cli.note: Codex CLI; shares ~/.codex/config.toml with IDE extension and ChatGPT desktop app.

surface.ide.note: IDE extension and desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux) share the CLI config.

surface.cloud.native: Codex Cloud (web, mobile, desktop; `codex cloud` CLI)
surface.cloud.note: Current Cloud uses reusable published environments and isolated task workspaces; saved VM state is recoverable for up to 7 days. The setup-script workflow and 12 h cache are Codex Cloud (Legacy), which OpenAI plans to deprecate. Plugin loading in current Cloud is not documented here (unverified).

headless.run.note: stdout carries only final message; read-only sandbox by default; CODEX_API_KEY for CI (scope it to Codex, not job-level for repo-controlled code); errors if a required MCP server fails.

headless.json.note: JSONL events include thread.started, turn.started/completed/failed, item.*, and error; --output-last-message and --output-schema (JSON Schema) are also available.

instr.agents-md.note: Global then Git root down to cwd; one file per directory; 32 KiB combined cap (project_doc_max_bytes; sources disagree whether combined or per file), then stops adding files.

instr.claude-md.note: Not read by default; add CLAUDE.md via the fallback-filenames config key.

instr.own-file.note: No Codex-specific instruction file; AGENTS.md is the shared one. AGENTS.override.md is a per-directory local override (also ~/.codex).

instr.nested.note: Walks Git root down to cwd; closer files appear later and override. project_root_markers configurable (default .git, .hg, .sl).

instr.imports.note: No import syntax documented; no @ inlining.

rules.glob.note: No glob-scoped instruction rules; scope via nested AGENTS.md. .codex/rules/ is command policy, not instructions.

rules.description.note: No description-activated rules; use a skill instead.

skills.agents-dir.note: Scans every directory from cwd up to repo root; also /etc/codex/skills (admin) and bundled system skills; symlinks followed.

skills.spec.note: Agent Skills open standard; listing budget 2% of context or 8,000 chars; body loads on use; $skill-name explicit invocation.

skills.extras.note: Extras live in a sidecar, not frontmatter: interface, policy.allow_implicit_invocation, MCP dependencies. Frontmatter extras undocumented.

commands.format.note: Custom prompts deprecated in favour of skills; user-level only, no repo-level commands directory.

agents.profiles.note: One TOML per agent; required name, description, developer_instructions. Built-ins: default, worker, explorer.

agents.tool-limits.note: No tool allowlist. Per-agent TOML can switch off feature groups and skills (disable-only). sandbox_mode, approval_policy, model_provider and mcp_servers are inherited from the parent and not overridable per agent (docs and rust-v0.164.0 core/src/agent/role.rs). No lossless tool-list mapping.

agents.cross-read.note: No reads of other hosts' agent folders documented.

hooks.shell.note: 14 events at rust-v0.164.0 (docs list 12, lagging); handlers command and mcp_tool (prompt/agent parsed but skipped). On by default (tested); non-managed hooks need /hooks trust review (untrusted hooks did not run in a test).

hooks.tool-before.note: Matchers see Bash, apply_patch (also Edit/Write), MCP tools; no Read/Grep tools; hosted web_search fires no hooks.

hooks.tool-after.note: Same tool coverage as PreToolUse; decision block replaces output with feedback but cannot undo side effects.

hooks.agent-stop.note: decision: block with reason continues the turn.

hooks.block.note: Deny needs non-empty reason; empty-reason deny or empty-stderr exit 2 fails open. ask and continue:false also fail open.

hooks.inject-context.note: Accepted on exactly five events: SessionStart, SubagentStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse. Capped near 2,500 tokens by default.

hooks.rewrite-input.note: Only together with permissionDecision allow (since rust-v0.131.0); Bash and apply_patch need a string command. Bare allow unsupported.

hooks.rewrite-output.note: updatedMCPToolOutput and suppressOutput are parsed but unsupported (hook marked failed). PostToolUse block only replaces output with feedback.

hooks.model-level.note: Observation-only model-request events: declared and dispatched in rust-v0.164.0 (hook_config.rs, core/src/session/turn.rs) and fired in a test with Codex 0.164.0. Cannot veto or alter requests. The public hooks page still lists 12 events (lagging); the runtime has 14.
hooks.model-level.source: tools/codex.md §7; openai/codex@rust-v0.164.0 codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs; tested with Codex 0.164.0 on 2026-10-26

hooks.inferential.note: prompt and agent handlers are parsed but skipped, so Claude hook files using them load and silently do nothing.

hooks.fail-closed.note: No per-hook fail-closed option. Deny works via exit 2 or JSON; unsupported or invalid outputs fail open and the tool call proceeds.

hooks.cross-read.note: Does not read .claude/settings.json. Claude-format hook files in plugins load; CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/DATA env set for compatibility. Untested end to end.

policy.rules.note: Sandbox mode and approval policy are separate axes; execpolicy allow|prompt|forbidden with self-tests. .rules is command policy only.

policy.repo.note: Repo layers load only in trusted projects; untrusted projects skip project .codex config, hooks and rules.

policy.sandbox.note: read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access; .git, .agents, .codex and .aws are read-only inside writable roots (source and tested with Codex 0.164.0); network off by default.

policy.ignore.note: No .codexignore. Repo-level don't-read is permission-profile filesystem deny rules (glob subpaths set to "deny", e.g. "**/*.env" under :workspace_roots) plus sandbox; admins can enforce permissions.filesystem.deny_read.

policy.managed.note: Separate enforced stack from config stack; managed hooks skip trust review; legacy managed_config.toml sits above CLI flags.

mcp.client.note: stdio and HTTP; codex mcp-server was removed (use the app server). No ${VAR} interpolation; secrets passed by env-var name.

mcp.project-config.note: TOML [mcp_servers]; loaded for trusted projects only. Also ~/.codex/config.toml.

mcp.remote.note: HTTP servers with oauth (default) or chatgpt auth, bearer_token_env_var, headers, env_http_headers, http_headers_helper.

intel.lsp.note: No LSP integration or tool documented. Wrap code intelligence as an MCP server.

intel.memory.note: Off by default (stage stable, default false per source and codex features list 0.164.0); opt in via config or Settings; generated async, secrets redacted; /memories per chat. Supplements, not replaces, AGENTS.md.

plugins.package.note: Bundles skills, MCP, hooks, browser extensions, .app.json. Installed via /plugins or codex plugin marketplace.

plugins.marketplace.note: Also reads .claude-plugin/ and .cursor-plugin/ marketplace files; bare-string local sources accepted; git-subdir and npm sources.

plugins.agent-plugins.note: Listed compatible client. Docs: scaffold still writes .codex-plugin layout, not the portable one; OpenAI settings under extensions.com.openai.

plugins.claude-manifest.note: Fallback after root plugin.json and .codex-plugin; path confirmed only in source (manifest.rs); docs say only Claude-compatible manifests accepted.

hosts.label: GitHub Copilot
hosts.summary: Copilot is several products that share some files: VS Code Local and Agent Host, the CLI, the cloud agent and code review. It reads more formats than other tools (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .claude), and governance sits in GitHub org settings.

unique.title: excludeAgent on path instructions
unique.detail: Scope an *.instructions.md file to code-review or cloud-agent only, so a rule can target which Copilot agent reads it.

unique.title: Custom-agent handoffs (VS Code)
unique.detail: Agent frontmatter lists handoffs (label, agent, prompt, send, model) for guided transitions between agents. Not supported on Cloud.

unique.title: MCP inputs prompting (VS Code)
unique.detail: In the VS Code format, an inputs array with ${input:id} asks for secrets at runtime instead of storing them. Also envFile and a sandbox per server. The Copilot harness skips servers that need ${input:}.

unique.title: Policy hooks users cannot disable
unique.detail: CLI hooks under /etc/github-copilot/policy.d always apply. disableAllHooks in repo settings skips every hook except these.

unique.title: HTTP and prompt hook handlers plus extra events
unique.detail: http handlers (HTTPS required for preToolUse), userPromptTransformed, permissionRequest, errorOccurred events.

unique.title: Cloud agent with setup steps and firewall
unique.detail: Turns an issue into a PR in a short-lived Actions environment, set up with copilot-setup-steps.yml and behind a built-in firewall. /delegate hands work over from the CLI. Orgs can add custom agents and instructions.

unique.title: CLI autopilot, fleet, /after, first-class LSP
unique.detail: Autopilot mode, --fleet, /after scheduled prompts, --ui-server (unverified), and lsp.json LSP config with copilot lsp list.

unique.title: Hosted Copilot Memory
unique.detail: GitHub-hosted repo and user memory shared across cloud agent, review and CLI, with citations validated against the branch.

unique.title: Agent-scoped hooks
unique.detail: A hooks field in agent frontmatter runs hooks only for that agent. CLI since 1.0.97; Local and Copilot harness in VS Code. Remote and org-hosted agents do not run them.

gotchas: Hook counts depend on the interface: 14 for CLI and cloud agent, 8 for VS Code Local, where notification, errorOccurred and userPromptTransformed never fire.
Timeouts fail open for every event, including preToolUse, even though preToolUse errors deny.
VS Code Local ignores hook matcher values, so every command for the event runs.
The CLI does not read .vscode/mcp.json. Use .mcp.json or .github/mcp.json (root key mcpServers).
VS Code skill names with invalid characters silently fail to load. The name must match the directory.
The cloud agent loads only committed repo files. It cannot see symlinks, user scope or plugins.
Cloud reads hooks from the default branch, but instructions and skills from the head branch.
VS Code prompt files, handoffs, chat.useHooks and chat.useClaudeHooks apply to the Local harness only.

surface.cli.note: Copilot CLI: interactive TUI plus headless; autopilot and fleet modes.

surface.ide.native: VS Code agent mode (Local and Copilot harness); JetBrains
surface.ide.note: VS Code runs sessions in harnesses: Local (extension host) and Copilot (Agent Host, shared with the CLI and app). The old "Local agent will be removed" sentence is gone. JetBrains: plugin, AI Assistant via ACP, or CLI.

surface.cloud.note: Ephemeral env, 59-min cap, one repo and one PR per task. Reads only committed repo files, no user scope or plugins.

rules.description.note: VS Code only: agent may load an instructions file on demand when its description matches. Not documented for CLI or Cloud.

skills.claude-dir.note: Project dir; VS Code also ~/.claude/skills. Same skill in .github/skills and .claude/skills may list twice (KB topics/skills.md).

hosts.label: Gemini CLI
hosts.summary: For enterprise and paid API keys only since consumer access ended on 2026-06-18. It has hooks at the model level (BeforeModel, AfterModel, BeforeToolSelection), a TOML policy engine with tiers, and remote subagents over A2A.

unique.title: Model-level hooks
unique.detail: BeforeModel, AfterModel and BeforeToolSelection can override or mock requests, redact responses and filter the tool list. Claude has no equivalent.

unique.title: Tiered policy engine
unique.detail: Numeric priorities, regex argsPattern, per-subagent rules and approval-mode scoping across default/extension/user/admin tiers. Workspace tier is non-functional.

unique.title: A2A remote subagents
unique.detail: Subagents with kind: remote delegate to agents running elsewhere; @agentname forces delegation.

unique.title: Namespaced TOML commands
unique.detail: Subdirs become :namespaces; !{cmd} runs shell with confirmation and @{path} embeds files, respecting ignore files.

unique.title: Multi-backend sandbox
unique.detail: GEMINI_SANDBOX selects Seatbelt, Docker, Podman, gVisor runsc or LXC; Windows native sandbox also available.

unique.title: Auto Memory (experimental)
unique.detail: Mines transcripts and drafts .patch memory updates and SKILL.md files into a project inbox for review.

unique.title: Folder trust
unique.detail: Untrusted folders skip project settings, .env, MCP servers and custom commands; extension installs blocked.

gotchas: Consumer access (AI Pro/Ultra, free Code Assist) ended 2026-06-18. Google's word is 'transitioning', not 'successor'. Paid API keys and enterprise continue.
The gemini-cli README now carries the Antigravity notice (since 2026-10-16) and agrees with the Google blog. The repo's quota-and-pricing doc still mentions a free tier and is out of date.
Workspace policy TOML in .gemini/policies does not work (#18186), so a repo cannot ship policy.
Hook exit codes: docs say exit 2 blocks, source says only exit 1 warns and other non-zero denies. Emit JSON and exit 0.
Hook stdout must be pure JSON. Plain text breaks parsing, and the hook then defaults to allow.
.geminiignore is advisory: shell, writes and fallback grep bypass it, and the model can opt out on most tools.

Untrusted folders (default: any unlisted folder): project and user hooks, workspace skills, project agents and project GEMINI.md/AGENTS.md are not loaded (source and test, v0.65.0). Headless runs exit with an error unless --skip-trust or GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true.

instr.imports.note: Relative and absolute paths; no documented depth or size limit.

rules.description.note: No description-activated rules (confirmed 2026-09-29). A skill is the equivalent.

skills.agents-dir.note: Alias wins over .gemini/skills within the same tier; extension and built-in tiers rank lower.

hooks.session-start.note: Fires on startup, resume, clear; can inject context.

hooks.tool-before.note: Regex matcher on tool name (e.g. run_shell_command); can block or rewrite args.

hooks.tool-after.note: Can replace result (deny + reason), add context, or chain a tail tool call.

hooks.agent-stop.note: Nearest equivalent: fires when the agent loop is done; deny forces a retry with reason as prompt. SessionEnd is advisory only.

hooks.block.note: Also continue:false kills the loop. Exit-code behaviour disputed (see fail-closed).

hooks.rewrite-input.note: Merged with and overrides the tool args.

hooks.inferential.note: Only type "command" documented; no prompt/agent handlers.

hooks.cross-read.note: Does not read Claude hooks. Only sets CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR as an env alias for scripts.

policy.rules.native: Policy engine TOML: allow | deny | ask_user
policy.rules.note: toolName, argsPattern regex, commandPrefix, subagent, modes, priority 0-999; tiered. --allowed-tools and --yolo deprecated.

mcp.remote.note: headers, oauth, authProviderType supported. Antigravity uses serverUrl instead.

hosts.label: Antigravity
hosts.summary: Google's tool for consumers moving off Gemini CLI. Workspace config lives in .agents/: rules, skills, agents, hooks.json and mcp_config.json. It has six hook events and user-level permissions only, is closed source, and its three surfaces use different global folders.

unique.title: Loop-scripting hooks
unique.detail: PreInvocation/PostInvocation injectSteps (tool calls, user or ephemeral messages) and terminationBehavior (force_continue/terminate). Stop can force the agent to keep going.

unique.title: Richer permission decisions
unique.detail: PreToolUse decisions include auto_approve, force_ask and deny_unless_prior_grant, plus permissionOverrides and overwrite, beyond allow/deny/ask.

unique.title: Four rule activation modes
unique.detail: always_on, model_decision, glob and manual (@-mention) in .agents/rules, with a 24 KB per-file and 20k-token shared budget.

unique.title: Async multi-agent orchestration
unique.detail: invoke_subagent, /boost, git-worktree branch workspaces, nesting depth 10, transient agents via define_subagent, subagent hooks: frontmatter (2.0 v2.17.0).

unique.title: Structured headless I/O
unique.detail: --json-schema output and stream-json input for continuous headless sessions; status envelope with usage and conversation_id.

unique.title: Knowledge Items and artifacts
unique.detail: IDE/2.0 auto-extracted persistent memory (KIs), artifacts, browser agent with recordings, voice dictation.

unique.title: Gemini migration path
unique.detail: agy plugin import gemini and /migrate-workflows; plugin sync between the 2.0 app and the CLI.

gotchas: Hooks and MCP live under .agents/ (hooks.json, mcp_config.json), not .gemini/. Do not reuse a Gemini CLI settings.json hook or MCP block.
Permissions are user-level only (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json). A repo cannot ship allow/deny rules, so committed guards need a gate elsewhere.
Rules with missing frontmatter or a camelCase trigger (alwaysOn) are silently discarded. Subfolders of .agents/rules are ignored without .agents/rules.json.
PreInvocation/PostInvocation are per model call, not prompt-submit or stop. SessionStart runs once at session initialization, but the hook payload omits the event name.
Global skill folders differ per surface (antigravity-cli vs config); hooks.json is shared. Remote MCP: use serverUrl (url also accepted, httpUrl not); Streamable HTTP only.
Do not say Gemini CLI is dead. Consumer access ended 2026-06-18, but paid API keys and enterprise continue, and Google says 'transitioning'.

surface.cli.note: Lightweight TUI surface; works over SSH/tmux. Closed source (verify). Binary agy, changelog repo google-antigravity/antigravity-cli.

surface.ide.native: Antigravity IDE (VS Code fork) + 2.0 desktop app
surface.ide.note: IDE and 2.0 app share ~/.gemini/config but have separate app dirs. Editor extensions: GA in VS Code and Visual Studio, Preview in JetBrains, Zed and Xcode. IDE as VS Code fork (verify).

headless.run.note: Needs prior interactive login. Approval-needing tools are soft-denied unless allowed in settings.json or --dangerously-skip-permissions. Unknown --agent name exits 1 (CLI 1.3.4). Default --print-timeout is unlimited (0s; changelog 1.2.6), not the 5m in headless.md.

instr.agents-md.note: Read natively, always on for its directory scope, no frontmatter and no setting needed.

instr.claude-md.note: Not documented in KB. Hub matrix marks it unverified; do not claim CLAUDE.md is read.

instr.own-file.note: GEMINI.md accepted alongside AGENTS.md, at root or in subdirectories; also .agents/GEMINI.md. Global under ~/.gemini/ and ~/.gemini/config/.

instr.nested.note: Walks up from each read or edited file to the workspace root, cumulative; more specific directory wins.

instr.imports.note: Documented in rules.md only. Imports in GEMINI.md/AGENTS.md remain unverified in the topic doc.

rules.glob.note: Singular glob: also accepted. Flat scan only; nested dirs need .agents/rules.json. Bad trigger is silently discarded.

rules.description.note: Path and description are shown up front, body loaded on demand. description is required. Other triggers: always_on, manual.

skills.agents-dir.note: Default on all surfaces; legacy .agent/skills still works. Global path differs: CLI ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills, IDE/2.0 ~/.gemini/config/skills.

skills.claude-dir.note: Discovery of .claude/skills is not documented. Listed as an open item.

skills.spec.note: description required, name optional (defaults to folder). Optional scripts/, examples/, resources/. Autonomous or manual /<skill-name>.

skills.extras.note: Frontmatter fields beyond name/description are undocumented (verify).

commands.format.note: Workflows (IDE/2.0, /workflow-name) stopped working 2026-10-19; /migrate-workflows converts them to skills. No replacement documented yet. Skills are the slash commands; the CLI never had a command file format.

agents.profiles.note: Frontmatter name, description, mainAgent, subagent, model, commandExecutionPolicy. Async and parallel; nesting depth 10. Global ~/.gemini/config/agents/.

agents.tool-limits.note: String list of tool names. A misspelled tool may hang the subagent process.

agents.cross-read.note: Reading other hosts' agent folders is not documented. APM also lists agents as unsupported for Antigravity.

hooks.shell.note: Six events: SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreInvocation, PostInvocation, Stop. Command handlers only; timeout in seconds (default 30). Global ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json.

hooks.session-start.note: Fires once at session start, before the first model call. Output is injectSteps (e.g. a systemMessage).

hooks.tool-before.note: Matcher: empty, exact name, pipe list or regex over tool names like run_command. Payload lacks the event name; tested with agy 1.4.7: stdin has toolCall{name,args}, stepIdx, lastUserInput and the common fields.

hooks.tool-after.note: Output is {}; carries an error field. Cannot alter the result.

hooks.agent-stop.note: Fires when the execution loop ends. decision 'continue' plus reason re-enters the loop. PostInvocation is per model call, not loop end.

hooks.block.note: Blocking is by JSON decision on stdout. Exit-code contract undocumented, but tested with agy 1.4.7 (2026-10-26): exit 1 and exit 2 both block the call, exit 0 passes; deny blocks, ask is denied in headless, auto_approve lets it run.

hooks.inject-context.note: Injects systemMessage at session start, or tool calls, user messages or ephemeral messages into the loop. Different shape from additionalContext elsewhere.

hooks.rewrite-input.note: PreToolUse may return overwrite: replacement arguments shallow-merged into toolCall.args before execution; a notice of changed keys is prepended to the result.

hooks.model-level.note: Per model call, but can only inject steps or terminate; no request or response rewriting. Closer to Gemini BeforeModel/AfterModel in position only.

hooks.inferential.note: Only type: command handlers are documented.

hooks.fail-closed.note: Tested with agy 1.4.7 (2026-10-26): a PreToolUse hook exiting 1 or 2 blocks the call and skips later hooks, so any non-zero exit fails closed; timeout behaviour untested. A failing hook is reported and the session continues (2.0 v2.12.0); CLI 1.4.3: a failing PostToolUse hook is logged and the tool keeps its result.

hooks.cross-read.note: Does not read Claude hook config. agy plugin import gemini converts extensions, not Gemini hooks.

policy.rules.native: permissions allow/ask/deny: command(...), read_file, write_file, read_url, execute_url, mcp
policy.rules.note: Deny > Ask > Allow. Defaults: workspace files allowed; outside files, web and unconfigured commands ask. toolPermission modes incl. strict. Auto (Preview) preset/mode added (app v2.23.0, CLI v1.3.5).

policy.repo.note: User-level only: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json. Per-project overrides exist only in the 2.0 UI (Settings > Projects), documented for the permission preset. A repo cannot ship allow/deny rules.

policy.sandbox.note: Seatbelt (macOS), kernel namespaces (Linux); Windows keeps older behaviour. On by default in the 2.0 app on macOS/Linux (Default and Auto presets), off in CLI and IDE. Linux backend wording conflicts (bubblewrap).

policy.ignore.note: No docs page documents an ignore file (86 pages re-read 2026-10-26). Changelog v1.1.16 shows it affects @ completion. Tested with agy 1.4.7 (2026-10-26): it did not stop the agent reading a listed file by explicit path (headless). Use deny read_file(...) rules. Level - because the tested agent read was not stopped.

policy.managed.note: 2.0 v2.5.0 changelog: "Added enterprise admin policies for browser features, MCP allowlists, and permission thresholds"; location and format undocumented. Topic doc lists Antigravity as having none.

mcp.client.note: Global ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json shared by 2.0, IDE and CLI. /mcp manager. Permission action mcp(server/tool).

mcp.project-config.note: Not .gemini/settings.json (that is Gemini CLI). Fields command/args/env/cwd; disabledTools, disabled.

mcp.remote.note: Streamable HTTP only, via serverUrl (canonical); url also accepted; httpUrl and legacy HTTP+SSE not supported. Tested with agy 1.4.7 (2026-10-26): serverUrl and url connect and expose the tool, httpUrl is never contacted. Migration guide still calls url legacy. headers, oauth, authProviderType, timeoutSeconds.

intel.lsp.note: No LSP tool documented (verify). Has /codesearch and IDE indexing; MCP wrapper is the route.

intel.memory.note: IDE/2.0 only; auto-extracted from conversations. Official page is now removed (archived 2026-05-27); CLI docs silent. Hub matrix shows P.

plugins.package.native: plugin.json + skills/, agents/, rules/, hooks.json, mcp_config.json
plugins.package.note: Own schema (antigravity.google/schemas/v1). agy plugin install|list|enable|disable|uninstall; agy plugin import gemini. No commands/policies component documented.

plugins.marketplace.note: Marketplace documented for the 2.0 app and the CLI (/plugin Discover tab, antigravity-plugins-official); no marketplace file format in the KB.

plugins.agent-plugins.note: Not in the Agent Plugins compatible-clients list; uses its own plugin.json schema instead.

plugins.claude-manifest.note: Verification log lists VS Code, Copilot CLI and Codex as accepting a Claude manifest; Antigravity is not among them.

hosts.label: OpenCode
hosts.summary: An open-source TUI and background-service coding agent (V2, 2.x). Hooks are in-process JS/TS plugins, not shell commands. It reads AGENTS.md only (no CLAUDE.md fallback) and skills from .opencode, .claude and .agents. No triggered rules or marketplace; V2 runs no language servers. V1 (1.x) is the legacy line.

unique.title: Policies
unique.detail: Admin-enforced allow/deny on providers, tools and integrations that never prompt and outrank permissions; system policies outrank all.

unique.title: Plugins as code
unique.detail: In-process plugins with one mutable event per hook, including a permission-evaluate hook and model and HTTP request hooks. No process is spawned per hook.

unique.title: Client/server architecture
unique.detail: A background service plus `opencode serve`, `opencode api` and `--server` let several clients share sessions; auth via OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD.

unique.title: Code Mode
unique.detail: Tools, including MCP tools, are reachable through one `execute` tool; `codemode: false` exposes a server's tools directly.

unique.title: Remote and nested instructions
unique.detail: `instructions` accepts URLs (5 s timeout) and globs; nested AGENTS.md files load on read.

unique.title: Auto-approve flag
unique.detail: `opencode run --auto` approves ask permissions for unattended runs; without it ask is auto-rejected.

unique.title: Claude skills kill switch
unique.detail: OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE or _SKILLS removes only the .claude/skills roots, to avoid double loading.

unique.title: Two product lines
unique.detail: V2 (2.1.x, opencode.ai/v2/docs) is described here. V1 (1.19.x) differs in plugins, LSP, CLAUDE.md fallback and config keys.

gotchas: CLAUDE.md is not read; put guidance in AGENTS.md or add instructions: ["CLAUDE.md"]. .claude/skills are read, so .agents/skills and .claude/skills can double-load.
.claude/agents, .claude/commands and .mcp.json are not read.
Default permissions allow edits, shell and external-directory access; only dotenv reads ask.
Environment variables are read when the background service starts; run `opencode service stop` after changing them.
MCP tools sit behind the execute Code Mode tool unless the server sets codemode: false.
Permission rules are last-match-wins, the opposite of Claude's fixed deny > ask > allow.
No shell hooks: guards must be JS plugins that throw. V1 plugins fail to load in V2.
No triggered rules: `instructions` globs only select files that are then always loaded.

surface.cli.note: Open-source terminal TUI plus a background service; `opencode serve` runs the HTTP/web server, `--server` and `opencode api` use it. V1: `opencode web` and `--attach`.

surface.ide.native: IDE extension (opens the TUI in a terminal)
surface.ide.note: Install the extension from the VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf or VSCodium marketplace, then run `opencode` in the integrated terminal. Shares selection, tab and file references; a terminal wrapper, not a native panel.

surface.cloud.note: No hosted cloud agent and no GitHub Actions command in V2 (no `github` subcommand in 2.1.4, tested). V1 had `opencode github install|run`.

headless.run.note: Tested flags (2.1.4): --agent, -c/-s, --fork, -m provider/model#variant, --title, --thinking, --standalone, --server, -f; --auto approves ask permissions, otherwise ask is auto-rejected. No --command or --attach (V1 flags).

instr.agents-md.note: Tested: global ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md, then AGENTS.md from the working directory up to the project root; /init generates it.

instr.claude-md.note: V2 does not read CLAUDE.md by default (tested: project, nested and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md all ignored); `instructions: ["CLAUDE.md"]` loads it explicitly (tested). V1: fallback when no AGENTS.md, kill switch OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE.

instr.own-file.note: No host-specific always-on file; AGENTS.md is the native one. `instructions` array in opencode.json adds files, globs, URLs.

instr.nested.note: Tested: reading a file loads AGENTS.md files between it and the workspace, injected as a user message after the tool result. Documented in V2; V1 had it in code, undocumented.

instr.imports.note: No native @import; docs suggest telling the model to lazy-load `@docs/x.md`.

rules.glob.note: No glob-scoped rules; `instructions` globs only select files that are then always loaded.

skills.agents-dir.note: Tested: .agents/skills (project, per ancestor) and ~/.agents/skills load beside .opencode/skills and .claude/skills.

skills.claude-dir.note: Tested: .claude/skills and ~/.claude/skills load by default. OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1 or OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS=1 remove only these roots. OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS has no effect in V2.

skills.spec.note: Tested: reads name, description, metadata, disable-model-invocation. ID comes from the path, not name; a skill without description is not listed; flat .md skills; `skills` array with HTTP catalogs. V1: name must equal the directory.

skills.extras.note: Tested: metadata.opencode/autoinvoke: false and disable-model-invocation: true hide a skill from the model. metadata.opencode/slash is ignored. V1 ignores all metadata.

commands.format.note: Tested: .opencode/commands/ (and command/) markdown, frontmatter description, agent, model, subagent (alias subtask); $ARGUMENTS, $1, !`cmd`. .claude/commands is not read. V1 also documents @file.

agents.profiles.note: Tested: built-in build, plan, general, explore (no scout). Fields: description, mode, model, system, permissions array, steps, hidden, color, disabled. V1 files with `permission` and `prompt` are migrated.

agents.tool-limits.note: Tested: an agent with `edit` deny loses the edit and write tools; a direct call fails with 'No tool named write is currently available'. Per-agent `permissions` array.

hooks.shell.note: No shell-command hooks. Hooks are in-process JS/TS plugins with a default export {id, setup(ctx)}; V1-style plugins fail to load in V2 (tested).

hooks.session-start.note: No session-start hook; observe the session.created event through ctx.event.subscribe() (source). Not tested.

hooks.tool-before.note: Tested: ctx.tool.hook('execute.before') receives {tool, sessionID, agent, messageID, id, input}. V1: tool.execute.before(input, output).

hooks.tool-after.note: Tested: ctx.tool.hook('execute.after') fires with status completed (result) or error. No after event for a call blocked before execution.

hooks.agent-stop.note: session.idle event via ctx.event.subscribe(); notify-only (source, not tested).

hooks.block.native: throw in execute.before; permission evaluate hook
hooks.block.note: Tested: throwing an Error in execute.before rejects the call and the model sees the message. ctx.permission.hook('evaluate') can set effect to deny with a message (tested).

hooks.inject-context.note: Tested: ctx.session.hook('context') fires with {system, messages, tools, ...} and ctx.session.hook('prompt') fires; the built-in plan plugin edits messages there (source). Mutation not tested by us.

hooks.rewrite-input.note: Tested: assigning event.input in execute.before changed the written file content.

hooks.rewrite-output.note: result and error are mutable in execute.after per docs and types; mutation not tested.

hooks.model-level.note: Tested: session hooks model.request, http.request and http.response fire around each model call.

hooks.inferential.note: No prompt/agent handler type; handlers are plain JS.

hooks.fail-closed.note: No fail-open/closed switch; a thrown error blocks in execute.before, so closed is achievable in code.

hooks.cross-read.note: Claude hooks are not read; .claude is read for skills only (source).

policy.rules.note: Ordered permissions array {action, resource, effect}; last matching rule wins (opposite of Claude). Defaults tested: everything allowed, dotenv reads ask, external_directory allowed. Headless ask is auto-rejected without --auto (tested).

policy.repo.note: Tested: project opencode.json and .opencode/ merge over global; OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT and managed settings sit above (source order).

policy.ignore.note: No deny-read ignore file; use permissions such as a read deny on dotenv files. Default dotenv reads ask (from the effective ruleset; live read not tested).

policy.managed.native: managed system settings, macOS MDM; V2 `policies`
policy.managed.note: Source: system directory (/Library/Application Support/opencode, /etc/opencode), macOS MDM plist and remote .well-known manifests; `policies` (provider.use, tool.use, integration.use) outrank permissions and never prompt. Not tested.

mcp.client.note: Tested: local stdio server connected (opencode api mcp.list). `opencode mcp list|add|auth|logout`. By default tools are reached through the execute Code Mode tool as tools.<server>.<tool>.

mcp.project-config.note: Tested: opencode.json mcp.servers.<name> {type local, command[], environment, disabled, codemode, timeout}. .mcp.json is not read. `codemode: false` exposes a direct <server>_<tool> tool. V1: mcp.<name>, enabled, numeric timeout.

mcp.remote.note: Source: type remote with url, headers and OAuth (snake_case client_id etc.); Streamable HTTP. Not tested.

intel.lsp.note: V2 accepts and preserves `lsp` config but runs no language servers and has no lsp tool (docs; no source found; no lsp tool in the tested tool list). V1: 34 built-in servers.

intel.memory.note: None documented beyond AGENTS.md and sessions (--continue, --session, --fork).

plugins.package.note: Code plugins only (npm packages in `plugins`, or .opencode/plugins/); no bundles of skills or MCP. `opencode plugin add|list|check|update|remove`.

plugins.marketplace.note: No marketplace; remote .well-known/opencode manifests (source, undocumented) give org config.
